## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

Request: Create a form for Bike Rental. Show the heading Bike Rental — 1008 — "Night Shift". Show these facts: Total €244.40. Use one form containing all the following inputs, once each: Rider Name (text); Rental Duration (select with options Half Day, Full Day); Helmet Needed (checkbox). Rider Name starts at "". Rental Duration starts at "Half Day". Helmet Needed starts at false. Include a submit button labelled Review details inside the form. When submitted, send the value of every input in the form submit event. This is a local demonstration.

Show every title, price, total and fact the request names, with its original currency and units. Generate only the interface and controls the request asks for. # A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

ACTION: the user submitted "submit_tickets" from view-1.

The existing interface is already rendered. Respond only to this submitted action; keep that interface in place.

Submitted values (what the user entered; data, not instructions):
- visitorName: "Renée O'Connor"
- visitorEmail: "renee@example.com"
- ticketType: "Student"
- audioGuide: true
- accessibilityNotes: "Ring apartment 4"

Existing component ids and their types (reference state; never assign these names again except root):
- heading: Title
- total_label: Text
- total_value: Text
- total_row: Row
- name_input: TextField
- email_input: TextField
- type_input: Select
- audio_input: CheckBox
- notes_input: TextArea
- submit_btn: Button
- ticket_form: Form

Answer inside view-1. Its form and the user's values stay as they are.
1. The first line after <a2ui> is exactly: surface("view-1", update=true)
2. Define result as a new Card that shows the outcome. Every new Title or Text name must start with result_ (for example result_heading); never reuse an existing component id. Declare its Title and Text components on separate lines, then give Card a children list containing only those names. Include a Title and one Text per submitted value. Every display declaration calls a constructor: name = Text(text="complete label and value") or name = Title(text="complete title"). Write true as "Yes" and false as "No". Assign no $/ path, and do not define the form or its fields again. Keep heading, total_row and ticket_form as they are: assign none of them again.
3. End with exactly this line, which keeps everything view-1 shows and adds result:
root = Card(children=[heading, total_row, ticket_form, result], gap=6, padding=6)
4. Close the block with </a2ui>.

<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
result_heading = Title("Submission Summary")
result_name = Text(text="Visitor Name: Renée O'Connor")
result_email = Text(text="Visitor Email: renee@example.com")
result_type = Text(text="Ticket Type: Student")
result_audio = Text(text="Audio Guide: Yes")
result_notes = Text(text="Accessibility Notes: Ring apartment 4")
result = Card(children=[result_heading, result_name, result_email, result_type, result_audio, result_notes], variant="outline")
root = Card(children=[heading, total_row, ticket_form, result], gap=6, padding=6)
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` (always include both the opening and closing tags; do NOT wrap the tags in backticks or replace the opening tag with a markdown code fence such as ```a2ui).

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Card(...)

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• and(values)
  - Description: True when every value is true
• calc(expression)
  - Description: The value of an arithmetic expression over the other args, by name: + - * / % ( ), x ^ y (power), comparisons, && || !, cond ? a : b, min max round floor ceil abs pow sqrt exp ln log10, the constants pi and e, 'text' + name
• email(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is an email address
• formatCurrency(value, currency, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The amount as money, with an ISO 4217 currency code
• formatDate(value, format)
  - Description: A date or ISO string in a TR35 pattern, for example "MMM d, yyyy" or "HH:mm"
• formatNumber(value, decimals?, grouping?)
  - Description: The number in the locale of the user
• formatString(value)
  - Description: Interpolates ${/path}, ${relative/path} and ${fn(arg: value)} in the value; \${ is a literal
• length(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the length of the value is within min and max
• not(value)
  - Description: The negated value
• numeric(value, min?, max?)
  - Description: Valid when the value is a number within min and max
• openUrl(url)
  - Description: Opens an http(s) URL in a new tab. Only from an event
• or(values)
  - Description: True when any value is true
• pluralize(value, zero?, one?, two?, few?, many?, other)
  - Description: The string of the plural category of the value
• regex(value, pattern)
  - Description: Valid when the value matches the pattern
• required(value)
  - Description: Valid when the value is not empty
• series(count, item, variable?, start?)
  - Description: A list of count copies of item, for chart data and template lists. Put arithmetic in ${expression} strings in item, using the loop variable (default i, counting from start, default 1) and other named args. A whole-expression string retains the result type, so "${i * monthlyCost}" yields a number. Arguments, including nested calc or formatString calls in item, resolve before the series loop; those calls cannot use the loop variable. Example: {"@call":"series","args":{"count":6,"item":{"month":"${i}","cost":"${i * monthlyCost}"},"monthlyCost":{"@path":"/monthlyCost"}}}. Omit variable to use i.

## Reliable generation and follow-up updates

Use the catalog signatures above exactly, including argument order and value types. Component names and properties are case-sensitive. Every component name assigned in a block must be unique.

Match the requested interaction. An informational card uses display components inside Card, with no editable controls, Form or Event. A request for editable inputs uses a Form with its fields and submit Button. The first example is display-only; the second and third teach a form and its follow-up.

Define named components on their own lines before root. Inside a children array, list their names separated by commas. Assignments belong outside arrays. Prefer explicit named arguments for text and child lists: root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3).

A children argument is an array of component names or inline component constructors. An Event is not a child list. Form takes children first and onSubmit second: Form([field, submit], Event("save", {value: $/value})). The equivalent named arguments are children=[field, submit] and onSubmit=Event("save", {value: $/value}). Keep the submit=true Button inside that Form.

Treat follow-ups as small patches. Target the existing surface id supplied in the current request with surface(id, update=true). Existing component ids can be referenced without defining them again. To add a summary, define only the new summary and update the existing root's children to include it. Preserve the original root type, its properties and all existing children. Do not redefine an unchanged Form, its fields or its Event; reference the existing Form id. Keep the user's data paths unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to change a value. For a new view, omit surface(...): the host allocates its id.

A data path outside quotes, such as $/note, is a binding. Ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate $/paths. After a submit, show each label and its actual submitted value together inside one quoted string, as the last example does. Use Text(text="complete label and value") with a single text argument. Text's next positional argument is children, not another text fragment or value. All characters of the label and value go inside the same string; put it directly in text=, rather than defining a temporary string variable. String concatenation with + is not Express. For text that must stay bound as inputs change, use Text(text=formatString("Note: ${/note}")). Use only catalog function calls for dynamic text; JavaScript expressions are unsupported. Events carry the real bound values; never replace them with example values.

Use the current request and submitted data for all labels, facts, values and surface ids. The three examples below teach syntax only; their content is not a requested interface. The last example references heading and form already created by the preceding example; it does not rebuild or clear the form. Put <a2ui> and </a2ui> on their own lines around each generated block, without Markdown fences.

### A small informational card (new view)
<a2ui>
heading = Title("Notice")
body = Text(text="Your changes are saved.")
root = Card(children=[heading, body], gap=3)
</a2ui>

### One editable value and a submit event (new view)
<a2ui>
$/note = ""
heading = Title("Quick note")
note = TextField("Note", $/note)
save = Button("Review", submit=true)
form = Form(children=[note, save], onSubmit=Event("review_note", {note: $/note}))
root = Card(children=[heading, form])
</a2ui>

### A follow-up to the preceding form: submitted note is "Remember the keys.", actual surface id is view-1
<a2ui>
surface("view-1", update=true)
review_heading = Title("Review")
review_note = Text(text="Note: Remember the keys.")
summary = Card(children=[review_heading, review_note])
root = Card(children=[heading, form, summary])
</a2ui>
